cases.question: What form is used to file a petition on behalf of a qualifying relative?
cases.answer: The Petition for Alien Relative (Form I-130) is used to file a petition on behalf of a qualifying relative.
cases.quote: A U.S. citizen, U.S. national, [1] or lawful permanent resident (LPR) may file a petition on behalf of a qualifying relative using the Petition for Alien Relative ( Form I-130 ), in accordance with the regulations and form instructions.

cases.question: When might an immediate relative beneficiary file an Application to Register Permanent Residence or Adjust Status (Form I-485)?
cases.answer: An immediate relative beneficiary who is in the United States may file an Application to Register Permanent Residence or Adjust Status (Form I-485) concurrently with the immigrant petition or after it is approved.
cases.quote: For example, since immediate relatives are not subject to numerical limitations on visa availability, an immediate relative beneficiary who is in the United States may file an Application to Register Permanent Residence or Adjust Status ( Form I-485 ) concurrently with the immigrant petition or after it is approved.

cases.question: Under what circumstances can the U.S. Department of State (DOS) accept and adjudicate a Form I-130 filed abroad?
cases.answer: The U.S. Department of State (DOS) may accept and adjudicate a clearly approvable Form I-130 filed abroad by a U.S. citizen petitioner for an immediate relative if the petitioner establishes exceptional circumstances or falls under blanket authorization criteria defined by USCIS.
cases.quote: USCIS has delegated [7] authority to DOS to accept and adjudicate a clearly approvable Form I-130 filed abroad by a U.S. citizen petitioner for an immediate relative [8] if the petitioner establishes exceptional circumstances or falls under blanket authorization criteria defined by USCIS.

cases.question: Under what circumstances might a Consular section accept local Form I-130 filings for emergency situations?
cases.answer: The Consular section may exercise its discretion to accept local Form I-130 filings for other emergency or exceptional circumstances of a non-routine nature, subject to the limitations set forth in 9 FAM 504.2-4(B)(1) paragraph f above.
cases.quote: The Consular section may exercise its discretion to accept local Form I-130 filings for other emergency or exceptional circumstances of a non-routine nature, subject to the limitations set forth in 9 FAM 504.2-4(B)(1) paragraph f above.

cases.question: What kind of events might lead to temporary blanket authorizations for consular officers to accept Form I-130 petitions?
cases.answer: In an event such as a natural disaster or prolonged or severe civil strife, USCIS may give blanket authorization to consular officers to accept and adjudicate clearly approvable Form I-130 immediate relative petitions from petitioners directly affected by such events.
cases.quote: In an event such as a natural disaster or prolonged or severe civil strife, USCIS may give blanket authorization to consular officers to accept and adjudicate clearly approvable Form I-130 immediate relative petitions from petitioners directly affected by such events.

cases.question: Do temporary blanket authorizations require consular officers to accept Form I-130 petitions?
cases.answer: These temporary blanket authorizations do not require, but rather, allow you to use your discretion to accept a Form I-130.
cases.quote: These temporary blanket authorizations do not require, but rather, allow you to use your discretion to accept a Form I-130.

cases.question: What is the minimum age a U.S. citizen must be for their parent to be classified as an immediate relative?
cases.answer: A U.S. citizen must be at least 21 years of age for their parent to be classified as an immediate relative.
cases.quote: An alien who is a spouse or child of a United States citizen, or a parent of a U.S. citizen at least 21 years of age, shall be classified as an immediate relative under INA 201(b) if the consular officer has received from DHS an approved Petition to Classify Status of Alien Relative for Issuance of an Immigrant Visa, filed on the alien's behalf by the U.S. citizen and approved in accordance with INA 204, and the officer is satisfied that the alien has the relationship claimed in the petition.

cases.question: What form is required to be filed for an alien to be classified as an immediate relative?
cases.answer: An approved Petition to Classify Status of Alien Relative for Issuance of an Immigrant Visa is required.
cases.quote: An alien who is a spouse or child of a United States citizen, or a parent of a U.S. citizen at least 21 years of age, shall be classified as an immediate relative under INA 201(b) if the consular officer has received from DHS an approved Petition to Classify Status of Alien Relative for Issuance of an Immigrant Visa, filed on the alien's behalf by the U.S. citizen and approved in accordance with INA 204, and the officer is satisfied that the alien has the relationship claimed in the petition.

cases.question: Under what circumstances would an immediate relative not be documented as such?
cases.answer: An immediate relative will not be documented as such if the U.S. citizen refuses to file the required petition, or if the immediate relative is also a special immigrant under INA 101(a)(27) (A) or (B) and not subject to any numerical limitation.
cases.quote: An immediate relative shall be documented as such unless the U.S. citizen refuses to file the required petition, or unless the immediate relative is also a special immigrant under INA 101(a)(27) (A) or (B) and not subject to any numerical limitation.

cases.question: What must the consular officer receive for the spouse of a deceased U.S. citizen to be entitled to immediate relative status?
cases.answer: The consular officer must receive an approved petition from the DHS or official notification of such approval.
cases.quote: The spouse of a deceased U.S. citizen, and each child of the spouse, will be entitled to immediate relative status after the date of the citizen's death provided the spouse or child meets the criteria of INA 201(b)(2)(A)(i) or of section 423(a)(1) of Public Law 107-56 (USA Patriot Act) and the Consular Officer has received an approved petition from the DHS which accords such status, or official notification of such approval, and the Consular Officer is satisfied that the alien meets those criteria.

cases.question: What public law is referenced regarding the spouse of a deceased U.S. citizen?
cases.answer: Public Law 107-56 (USA Patriot Act) is referenced.

cases.question: What is the deadline for a child of a U.S. citizen victim of the September 11, 2001, terrorist actions to file a petition for immediate relative status?
cases.answer: The child must file a petition for such status within two years of the citizen's death.
cases.quote: The child of a U.S. citizen slain in the terrorist actions of September 11, 2001, shall retain the status of an immediate relative child (regardless of changes in age or marital status) if the child files a petition for such status within two years of the citizen's death pursuant to section 423(a)(2) of Public Law 107-56, and the consular officer has received an approved petition according such status or official notification of such approval.

cases.question: Who retains the authority to accept and adjudicate a local Form I-130 filing abroad?
cases.answer: USCIS retains authority to accept and adjudicate a local Form I-130 filing abroad.
cases.quote: Although USCIS has delegated authority to DOS to accept Form I-130 petitions in all locations abroad in the limited instances described above, USCIS retains authority to accept and adjudicate a local Form I-130 filing abroad or conduct an in-person interview abroad as warranted, regardless of where or how the petition was filed.

cases.question: What happens if multiple Form I-130 petitions for the same beneficiary and classification are approved?
cases.answer: If a Form I-130 petition and subsequent Form I-130 petition filed by the same petitioner for the same beneficiary and for the same classification are approved, USCIS regards the subsequent petition approval as a reaffirmation or reinstatement of the validity of the first petition.
cases.quote: If a Form I-130 petition and subsequent Form I-130 petition filed by the same petitioner for the same beneficiary and for the same classification are approved, USCIS regards the subsequent petition approval as a reaffirmation or reinstatement of the validity of the first petition.

cases.question: When is the original priority date retained for multiple Form I-130 petitions?
cases.answer: The original priority date is retained unless the original petition was terminated by the DOS, had its approval revoked, or a visa has been issued based on the original petition.
cases.quote: The original priority date is retained unless the original petition was terminated by the DOS, [20] had its approval revoked, [21] or a visa has been issued based on the original petition.

cases.question: What happens if an adoption-based Form I-130 is filed with other Form I-130s for additional relative beneficiaries?
cases.answer: If an adoption-based Form I-130 is filed along with any Form I-130 for additional relative beneficiaries, the adoption-based Form I-130 is adjudicated apart from the other family-based Form I-130s.
cases.quote: If an adoption-based Form I-130 is filed along with any Form I-130 for additional relative beneficiaries, the adoption-based Form I-130 is adjudicated apart from the other family-based Form I-130s.

cases.question: What form is prohibited from approval if an alien beneficiary has attempted or conspired to enter into a fraudulent marriage?
cases.answer: USCIS is barred from approving Form I-140 if the beneficiary has attempted or conspired to enter into a fraudulent marriage.
cases.quote: Accordingly, if an alien is a beneficiary of an Immigrant Petition for Alien Workers ( Form I-140 ) or a Petition for Amerasian, Widow(er) or Special Immigrant ( Form I-360 ), and the beneficiary has attempted or conspired to enter into a fraudulent marriage, USCIS is also be barred from approving the Form I-140 petition.

cases.question: What is the citation for the regulation that defines when an alien has been placed into proceedings and when proceedings are terminated?

cases.question: What must the record contain to apply the marriage fraud bar according to Matter of Pak?
cases.answer: The record must contain substantial and probative evidence of prior marriage fraud.
cases.quote: See Matter of Pak , 28 I&N Dec. 113 (BIA 2020) (the record must contain substantial and probative evidence of prior marriage fraud).

cases.question: Does INA 204(c) require the filing of a previous spousal petition or the existence of a prior marriage?
cases.answer: No, INA 204(c) does not require the filing of a previous spousal petition or the existence of a prior marriage.

cases.question: What provides a clear and substantial basis for applying the INA 204(c) bar?
cases.answer: A final order of deportation based on a marriage fraud finding provides a clear and substantial basis for applying the INA 204(c) bar.

cases.question: What form must a consular officer receive from DHS for an alien to be classified as a family-sponsored immigrant?
cases.answer: A consular officer must receive a Petition to Classify Status of Alien Relative for Issuance of Immigrant Visa from DHS.
cases.quote: An alien shall be classifiable as a family-sponsored immigrant under INA 203(a) (1), (2), (3) or (4) if the consular officer has received from DHS a Petition to Classify Status of Alien Relative for Issuance of Immigrant Visa approved in accordance with INA 204 to accord the alien such preference status, or official notification of such an approval, and the consular officer is satisfied that the alien has the relationship to the petitioner indicated in the petition.

cases.question: What is the minimum age requirement for a petitioner filing for an alien status under INA 203(a)(4) on or after January 1, 1977?
cases.answer: The petitioner must be at least twenty-one years of age for a petition to accord an alien status under INA 203(a)(4) filed on or after January 1, 1977.
cases.quote: In the case of a petition to accord an alien status under INA 203(a)(4) filed on or after January 1, 1977, the petitioner must be at least twenty-one years of age.

cases.question: Under which INA sections can an alien be classified as a family-sponsored immigrant?
cases.answer: An alien can be classified as a family-sponsored immigrant under INA 203(a) (1), (2), (3) or (4).
cases.quote: An alien shall be classifiable as a family-sponsored immigrant under INA 203(a) (1), (2), (3) or (4) if the consular officer has received from DHS a Petition to Classify Status of Alien Relative for Issuance of Immigrant Visa approved in accordance with INA 204 to accord the alien such preference status, or official notification of such an approval, and the consular officer is satisfied that the alien has the relationship to the petitioner indicated in the petition.

cases.question: Who is entitled to derivative status as a child of a family-sponsored immigrant?
cases.answer: The child of a family-sponsored first, second, third or fourth preference immigrant is entitled to derivative status.
cases.quote: Pursuant to INA 203(d), and whether or not named in the petition, the child of a family-sponsored first, second, third or fourth preference immigrant or the spouse of a family-sponsored third or fourth preference immigrant, if not otherwise entitled to an immigrant status and the immediate issuance of a visa, is entitled to a derivative status corresponding to the classification and priority date of the beneficiary of the petition.

cases.question: Who is entitled to derivative status as the spouse of a family-sponsored immigrant?
cases.answer: The spouse of a family-sponsored third or fourth preference immigrant is entitled to derivative status.

cases.question: What form is used for a Petition for Alien Relative?
cases.answer: The Form I-130 is used for a Petition for Alien Relative.
cases.quote: Consular officers can accept and adjudicate a clearly approvable Form I-130, Petition for Alien Relative, filed by a U.S. citizen who is a U.S. government or military employee assigned to a U.S. mission abroad under Chief of Mission authority or at an office of the American Institute in Taiwan, or a military service member stationed abroad, for any immediate relative.

cases.question: Do exceptional circumstances need to be present for a U.S. citizen government or military employee to file a Form I-130 overseas?
cases.answer: No, exceptional circumstances are not required for a U.S. citizen government or military employee to file a Form I-130 overseas.
cases.quote: Exceptional circumstances are not required, and you do not need to seek permission from USCIS to accept a Form I-130 filed under these circumstances.

cases.question: What must be confirmed before accepting a Form I-130 from a U.S. citizen government or military employee overseas?
cases.answer: Before acceptance, it must be confirmed that the petitioner has not previously filed a Form I-130 on behalf of the beneficiary with USCIS domestically or electronically.
cases.quote: Before acceptance, you must confirm that the petitioner has not previously filed a Form I-130 on behalf of the beneficiary with USCIS domestically or electronically.

cases.question: What must a petitioner file before filing an I-129F petition for a K-3 visa?
cases.answer: The petitioner must first file an I-130 Petition for an Alien Relative with USCIS.
cases.quote: To file an I-129F petition for a K-3 visa, the petitioner must first file an I-130 Petition for an Alien Relative with USCIS.

cases.question: What happens to the approval of a K visa petition if the petitioner dies before the beneficiary arrives in the United States?
cases.answer: The death of a petitioner before the arrival of the beneficiary in the United States automatically terminates the approval of the petition.
cases.quote: USCIS regulations (8 CFR 214.2(k)) provide that the death of a petitioner or written withdrawal of the petition before the arrival of the beneficiary in the United States automatically terminates the approval of the petition.

cases.question: What should be done with an inactive petition if no response is received within 60 days after its expiration?
cases.answer: The petition should be treated as inactive and destroyed after one year.
cases.quote: If the petition has not been automatically terminated but the applicant chooses not to pursue the visa while the petition is still valid (or if no response is received within 60 days if the petition has expired and the applicant does not respond to your letter per 9 FAM 502.7-3(C)(2) paragraph b below), the petition should be treated as inactive and destroyed after one year.

cases.question: Where should the notation for a revalidated K visa petition be placed?
cases.answer: The notation "Revalidated to (date)" should be placed in the "Remarks" block of the petition over your signature and title.
cases.quote: When a K visa petition is revalidated as described in 9 FAM 502.7-3(B) paragraph d(1)(b) above, the notation “Revalidated to (date)” should be placed in the “Remarks” block of the petition over your signature and title.

cases.question: What regulation covers the requirements for an abused adopted child to self-petition under the family-based process?
cases.answer: The requirements for an abused adopted child to self-petition under the family-based process are covered by INA 101(b)(1)(E), INA 204(a)(1)(A)(iv), and INA 204(a)(1)(B)(iii).
cases.quote: The requirements to self-petition as an abused adopted child apply to the family-based process under INA 101(b)(1)(E) , INA 204(a)(1)(A)(iv) , and INA 204(a)(1)(B)(iii) .
cases.citation: Volume 3, Part D, Chapter 2 - Eligibility Requirements and Evidence

cases.question: Under which section of the INA is an immediate relative entitled to status?
cases.answer: An immediate relative is entitled to status under INA 201(b).
cases.quote: an immediate relative entitled to status under 201(b)

cases.question: Under which sections of the INA is a family-sponsored immigrant entitled to preference status?
cases.answer: A family-sponsored immigrant is entitled to preference status under INA 203(a)(1)-(4).
cases.quote: a family-sponsored immigrant entitled to preference status under 203(a)(1)-(4)

cases.question: Under which sections of the INA is an employment-based preference immigrant entitled to status?
cases.answer: An employment-based preference immigrant is entitled to status under INA 203(b)(1)-(5).
cases.quote: an employment-based preference immigrant entitled to status under INA 203(b)(1)-(5)

cases.question: What must a consular officer receive before issuing a visa for immediate relative or preference status?
cases.answer: The consular officer must receive a petition filed and approved in accordance with INA 204 or official notification of such filing and approval.
cases.quote: unless the officer has received a petition filed and approved in accordance with INA 204 or official notification of such filing and approval.
